# Ensure that the proxy-usage-analysis is scripted as much as possible (LP-0MTY7CCQP002DOZ5)

## Headline

Retire the last LLM/agent step in the proxy-usage-analysis daily path: the
analysis pipeline is already fully deterministic (a ~5,200-line Python
script set) and the 05:00 cron already runs it unattended, so the remaining
work is to remove the herdr **scheduled-prompt** dispatch that puts an agent
in the daily loop and to reduce the skill definition to a thin, CLI-focused
wrapper around the script.

## Problem statement

The proxy-usage-analysis report is generated by a fully deterministic Python
pipeline, yet its daily cadence is still driven by an LLM agent: the herdr
downtime worker dispatches `/skill:proxy-usage-analysis --priority high`
once a day (LP-0MT2UKC26000D8YM), which starts an agent whose only job is to
invoke the same script the 05:00 cron (LP-0MSI8W67N007RJIL) already runs.
The agent contributes no analysis of its own — the script produces the
report, the CSVs, and the recommendations — so the dispatch is redundant
overhead (agent tokens, an extra same-day archive like
`~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-14_2/_3`, and a second code path to reason
about) with no operator-visible benefit. "Scripted as much as possible"
therefore means removing that last agent step, not re-scripting the
already-deterministic analysis.

## Users

- **rgardler (operator)** — wants the daily proxy-usage report produced
  hands-off by a non-interactive command, with no agent in the loop.
  - *User story:* "As the operator, I want the daily proxy report to be
    produced by a single scheduled script invocation (the 05:00 cron), so
    that the analysis is deterministic, cheap, and needs no agent or LLM to
    run."
  - *User story:* "As the operator, I still want to be able to run the
    analysis on demand via `/skill:proxy-usage-analysis` and have that
    simply invoke the CLI."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1 — Daily path is agent-free.** The daily proxy-usage report is
  produced solely by the existing 05:00 cron
  (`python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`),
  and `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` contains **no** `proxy-usage-analysis`
  entry — the LLM/agent dispatch (LP-0MT2UKC26000D8YM) is retired. No other
  agent/LLM step remains in the daily path.
- [x] **AC2 — Agent-free path is verified and recorded.** A repeatable,
  documented check (e.g. `grep` over `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/`,
  plus inspection of `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` and `crontab -l`)
  demonstrates that the cron is the sole trigger and no dispatch entry
  remains; the observed command + result is captured in a comment on this
  work item.
- [x] **AC3 — SKILL.md is a thin, CLI-focused wrapper.** The skill definition
  documents the non-interactive invocation and the 05:00 cron as the trigger,
  with agent-orchestration/imperative narration (e.g. the "EXECUTE
  immediately — do NOT ask permission or confirm" framing and any
  scheduler-dispatch references) removed. Substantive reference material that
  remains useful (report interpretation, root-cause taxonomy, limitations) is
  **retained or relocated to a linked doc**, not silently discarded.
- [x] **AC4 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.**
- [x] **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **No change to the analysis itself.** The deterministic pipeline
  (`analyze_proxy_usage.py`, `aggregation.py`, `bucketing.py`,
  `recommendations.py`, `reporting.py`, `log_parser.py`, `llama_log_parser.py`)
  is out of scope; this item touches only the *invocation/cadence* and the
  *skill definition*.
- **No new code path.** The daily path must remain a single CLI invocation;
  do not add a wrapper script unless one is strictly required (the CLI
  already exists and the cron already calls it).
- **Runtime config, not committed.** `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` is a
  gitignored, per-project runtime config (absent ⇒ empty set, malformed ⇒
  empty set). Removing the entry is a local runtime edit, not a committed
  artifact.
- **Project-local only.** The skill exists only at
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (relocated from global by
  LP-0MSDFAFX0000SKQK); do not touch `~/.pi/agent/skills/`.
- **Preserve on-demand usability.** `/skill:proxy-usage-analysis` must
  continue to work as a manual, on-demand entry point to the CLI.
- **UK English** in all brief/docs prose.

## Existing state

- **Analysis pipeline — already fully scripted.** ~5,200 lines of
  deterministic Python behind `scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`, with a test
  suite under `tests/` (`test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`,
  `test_llama_log_parser.py`). Every report section — session summary,
  hourly busy table, total tokens, fallback reasons, error taxonomy,
  root-cause breakdown, compaction, TTFT, decode/prompt-eval speed,
  recommendations — is produced by rule-based code, not by an LLM.
- **Root-cause classification — already automated.** The one section
  previously described as a manual investigation was automated on
  2026-10-13 (LP-0MUQO82LJ008F1FS, LP-0MUQO862C004UT7T): `root_cause` is now
  a deterministic field in `errors.csv` / `errors.json` and the report's
  root-cause table.
- **Unattended cadence — already exists.** The 05:00 cron runs the script
  with output appended to `~/proxy-usage-reports/cron.log`, archiving each
  day's artifacts automatically (LP-0MSI8W67N007RJIL). Confirmed live in
  `crontab -l` and daily archives under `~/proxy-usage-reports/`.
- **The only agent step — the scheduled prompt.** `herdr`'s downtime worker
  dispatches `/skill:proxy-usage-analysis --priority high` once a day from
  `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (`lastTriggeredAt`
  2026-10-14T13:59:57.981Z). The dispatched agent's only action is to run the
  same script — hence the redundancy (evidenced by same-day archives such as
  `2026-10-14_2` and `2026-10-14_3`).
- **SKILL.md framing.** The skill is written as an agent-invoked slash
  command ("EXECUTE immediately via /skill:proxy-usage-analysis; do NOT ask
  permission or confirm") even though the substantive work is the CLI.

## Desired change

1. **Retire the agent dispatch (scope decision 1a).** Remove the
   `proxy-usage-analysis` entry from `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` so
   the herdr downtime worker no longer spawns an agent for the daily report.
2. **Confirm the cron is the sole daily trigger (definition of done 2a).**
   The existing 05:00 cron already yields "a single non-interactive command
   produces the daily report with no agent/LLM in the loop".
3. **Thin the skill definition.** Rewrite `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`
   to a CLI-focused wrapper: non-interactive invocation + cron as the
   trigger; remove agent-orchestration narration; retain/relocate the
   substantive reference material (interpretation, taxonomy, limitations).

No new capability is added and no analysis behaviour changes — the change is
the removal of a redundant agent step plus the corresponding documentation
clean-up.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — Remove the `proxy-usage-analysis` entry
  (gitignored runtime config; local edit only).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` — Reduce to a thin, CLI-focused
  wrapper; drop agent-orchestration/imperative narration; retain or relocate
  reference sections.
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/` — Reference only (archives + `cron.log`) for AC2
  verification evidence; no edits.
- `crontab` (user crontab) — Reference only for AC2 verification; the cron
  entry is already present (LP-0MSI8W67N007RJIL) and unchanged.

## Related work

### find-related report (automated)

The `/skill:find-related` scan returned three items by keyword overlap —
**LP-0MNWBTFDL009MJOS** (Logs Observability & Access), **LP-0MTVJF5HU007ISP1**
(Fix local summarizer timeout causing compaction failures), and
**LP-0MQR7AYXB006XPQ6** (Implementation roadmap & handoff) — all completed.
These are keyword-noise matches with no bearing on this item (they concern
log access, summariser timeouts, and a roadmap, not reporting cadence). Its
repository matches were likewise noise (large `ds4/.../rendered_prompts*.txt`
datasets). The meaningful related work is the curated list below.

### Curated related work items

- **LP-0MT2UKC26000D8YM** — Add project-local scheduled prompt for
  proxy-usage-analysis (completed). The dispatch being retired here.
- **LP-0MSI8W67N007RJIL** — Archive proxy usage reports: auto-archive on each
  run + daily 05:00 cron (completed). The retained, agent-free mechanism.
- **LP-0MUQO82LJ008F1FS** / **LP-0MUQO862C004UT7T** — Classify stream-finish
  error root causes / adoption-aware stream-error recommendation and taxonomy
  (completed 2026-10-13). Automated the last previously-manual report
  section, making the pipeline fully deterministic.
- **LP-0MUIEO6IP0030CT3** — proxy-usage-analysis: exclude `chain_hold_cycle>0`
  re-emissions from local-skip demand counters (completed). Recent
  deterministic-analysis work.
- **LP-0MSDFAFX0000SKQK** — Relocate proxy-usage-analysis skill from global
  `~/.pi/agent/skills` to project-local `.pi/skills` (completed). Confirms
  the project-local-only constraint.
- **WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX** — herdr scheduled-prompts feature (framework repo;
  not in this store). The mechanism whose entry is removed.
- **LP-0MTYARXXZ002VNF5**, **LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS**, **LP-0MTHCTLAF00147IT** —
  Recent deterministic report extensions (log discovery, hourly bucketing,
  compaction reporting); evidence the pipeline is scripted.

## Risks

- **Documentation loss.** "Thin wrapper" could drop genuinely useful
  reference prose (root-cause taxonomy, limitations, interpretation guide).
  *Mitigation:* AC3 requires retention/relocation, not silent deletion.
- **Loss of the agent-curated summary.** Scope (1a) explicitly accepts that
  the daily report is the raw script output; no LLM narrative is produced.
  *Mitigation:* accepted by producer decision; the script's stdout summary +
  `report.md` remain.
- **Silent cron failure.** Without the daily agent as a second caller, a cron
  failure would go unnoticed. *Mitigation:* out of scope here — note as
  linked follow-up if desired (`cron.log` already records failures).
- **Scope creep.** Securing the agent-free path could tempt further pipeline
  changes. *Mitigation:* constraints confine the change to invocation +
  skill docs.
- **Idempotence of the runtime edit.** A re-run must not fail on an already
  absent entry. *Mitigation:* removal is a no-op when absent.

## Assumptions

- The 05:00 cron remains the intended daily mechanism (confirmed via
  `crontab -l` and LP-0MSI8W67N007RJIL).
- The scheduled-prompt entry is no longer wanted for this skill
  (producer decision 1a).
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/cron.log` remains the operational failure record.
- No CI/CD pipeline test changes are required (per intake guidance, CI/CD
  pipeline tests are excluded).
- The work-item title retains the original spelling "proxy-useage-analysis"
  (as authored); the brief uses the corrected term "proxy-usage-analysis".

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Round 1 — 2026-09-26 (original intake attempt; unanswered at the time)

- Q (2026-09-26): "Scope — what still counts as 'not scripted'? (a) replace
  the LLM-driven daily invocation with a direct non-interactive script/cron
  call; (b) accept as already scripted and close; (c) automate remaining
  manual sections (e.g. root-cause classification)." — **Answer: deferred**
  (no answer recorded during the first session). Context: option (c) was
  independently delivered on 2026-10-13 (LP-0MUQO82LJ008F1FS /
  LP-0MUQO862C004UT7T). Re-asked as Q1 in Round 2.
- Q (2026-09-26): "Definition of done — what observable outcome proves
  'scripted as much as possible'?" — **Answer: deferred.** Re-asked as Q2 in
  Round 2.
- Q (2026-09-26): "Trigger/context — what prompted this item now? Any case
  where the LLM-driven invocation produced inconsistent/incomplete output
  versus the 05:00 cron?" — **Answer: deferred.** Re-asked as Q3 in Round 2.

### Round 2 — 2026-10-14 (producer answered)

- Q1: "Scope: (a) retire the LLM-in-the-loop daily dispatch (rely on the
  05:00 cron only, remove the `proxy-usage-analysis` entry from
  `scheduled-prompts.json`, thin SKILL.md); (b) accept current state and
  close; (c) script a specific remaining step?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-10-14): (a).** Source: interactive reply. Research: verified the
  pipeline is deterministic and the root-cause taxonomy was automated
  2026-10-13, leaving the scheduled-prompt dispatch as the only agent step.
- Q2: "Definition of done: (a) a single non-interactive command (the
  existing CLI via cron) produces the daily report; no agent/LLM in the loop;
  `scheduled-prompts.json` no longer contains the entry; SKILL.md documents
  only the CLI with no agent-narration steps; (b) keep the scheduled prompt
  and add an audit checklist?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-14): (a).**
  Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Trigger: (a) a specific incident where the LLM-driven invocation
  produced inconsistent/incomplete output versus the 05:00 cron; (b) general
  hygiene — no specific incident?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-14): (b),
  general hygiene.** Source: interactive reply. Evidence for the underlying
  redundancy: same-day duplicate archives (`2026-10-14_2`, `2026-10-14_3`
  under `~/proxy-usage-reports/`).

## Goal (user story)
As a proxy operator, when a long agent session runs, its requests must keep progressing. A request must never sit in a remote fallback tier for 15 minutes and die with a 900-second timeout, and must never be blocked by local slot-accounting errors.

## Symptoms observed 2026-09-14
- pi session herdr-1789404733-1187468-16836 received "We were unable to start processing your request within the 900-second timeout limit. Please try again later." six times between 19:18 and 20:46 (about 17-18 min apart).
- dispatch_first_byte_ms: p50 4.6 s, p90 40 s, p99 212 s, max 713 s.
- 1982 routing_skip_local reason=context_too_large, 2341 fallbacks, 503 local_dispatch_denied, 811 counter-recovery warnings.

## Root causes (diagnosed this session)
1. Local dispatch accounting resets the generating counter mid-stream on a 1-slot backend (LP-0MU1RXEGB002CAL4).
2. Remote fallback stalls 240 s on opencode-go and retries empty upstream responses without a bound (LP-0MU1RXEPL005CK97).
3. The local large-context routing threshold does not scale with the per-slot capacity now that the profile runs one slot (LP-0MU1RXF6R004S8XL).
4. Proxy compaction fails 100 percent (summarizer_failed) and pushes sessions to remote_with_guidance (LP-0MU1RXEY10075TUU).

## Related existing work - do NOT duplicate
- LP-0MTXCQA8I0038J4X [CRITICAL] Dedicated small summarizer model for proxy-side session compaction - in-progress. This is the specialist model item; the compaction root cause above is largely owned by it plus the items below.
- LP-0MTT0O74N009E7N2 Add 'compact' model (Muse to DeepSeek) and wire proxy-side compaction to it - in-progress.
- LP-0MTVJF5HU007ISP1 Fix local summarizer timeout causing compaction failures - blocked by LP-0MTT0PB6J0053BPP.
- LP-0MTT0PB6J0053BPP Increase compaction_summarizer_timeout to 120s - open.
- LP-0MTY8Y1VB006IYGQ Per-model compaction trigger configuration - open.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No request in a 24 h post-change window returns the upstream 900-second queue-timeout error.
- [ ] dispatch_first_byte_ms p99 is below 60 s for local-routed requests.
- [ ] Zero local_generating_queries counter-recovery false positives while a stream is in flight.
- [ ] Compaction succeeds and is durable for sessions above the trigger (coordinates with the specialist model item rather than reimplementing it).
- [ ] The large-context routing threshold is an intentional, documented value for the 1-slot profile.
- [ ] Full test suite green.

## Non-goals
- Adding a new summariser model (owned by LP-0MTXCQA8I0038J4X).
- Renaming deepseek model identifiers (LP-0MU1RXFNO00552VR, pending a scope decision).

# Intake Brief: When a request cannot be processed because there are no available models include a retry timer (LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI)

## Headline

Verify, end-to-end, that when the proxy cannot process a request because every
model is unavailable it returns the "All providers exhausted" 503 carrying a
truthful retry timer (a `Retry-After` header and a matching `retry_after` body
field derived from real availability), and that the client can actually act on
it. The proxy emission is already implemented by the overnight-exhaustion epic;
this item proves the composed contract and tracks the one remaining client-side
gap (the 60 s clamp) in a linked ContextHub work item.

## Problem statement

Clients reach an upstream LLM through this proxy. When every provider that can
serve a request is unavailable — in cooldown, outside its `available_times`
window, or usage-limit quarantined — the proxy rejects the request with a 503
whose `error` prose is `"All providers exhausted"`. For an unattended agent
(herdr worker / Pi session) to recover automatically, that rejection must tell
it *how long* to wait, and the client must actually wait that long.

The proxy side was delivered by the overnight-exhaustion epic
(LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO): the generic and time-window exhaustion 503s emit a
`Retry-After` header plus a matching `retry_after` body field computed by
`_compute_retry_after` from real availability (cooldowns, window edges,
usage-limit resets). What is not owned anywhere is a single **end-to-end
verification** that the composed "no models available" retry contract holds and
fails if any part regresses. Separately, the client clamps an applied
`Retry-After` to 60 s (`retry-logic.ts` `maxDelayMs = 60000`), so a truthful
multi-hour overnight `retry_after` is never actually waited out — this needs a
linked ContextHub change.

## Users

- **Local agent (herdr worker / Pi session)** — the primary beneficiary. Must
  receive a truthful retry timer and be able to wait until models return instead
  of surfacing `Unrecognized error:` or retrying every 60 s through an
  overnight gap.
- **Proxy operator / on-call engineer** — needs confidence that any regression
  in the exhaustion retry contract is caught by an automated end-to-end test.
- **ContextHub maintainers** — need the client-side gap recorded and linked
  (WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM) so the proxy's honest timer is honoured.

### Example user stories

- As a local agent, I want the "All providers exhausted" 503 to carry a truthful
  `Retry-After`/`retry_after` so I know when to come back.
- As an operator, I want an end-to-end test that fails if the retry timer is
  dropped or becomes untruthful (e.g. hardcoded 60 s, or 0 while providers are
  blocked).
- As a ContextHub maintainer, I want the 60 s clamp tracked so the client waits
  out a multi-hour retry hint.

## Scope (producer-confirmed)

Per the producer's answers to the intake questions (Appendix):

- **Q1 = (b):** this item is an **end-to-end verification** of the whole
  "no models available" retry contract **on the proxy** (not a new feature that
  adds retry hints to further paths).
- **Q2 = (b):** the contract in scope is **only the "All providers exhausted"
  503** (generic `code: all_exhausted` and its time-window variant
  `code: outside_time_window`). The local slot-exhaustion 429 and the router
  concurrency-limit 503 are **out of scope**.
- **Q3 = (a):** the proxy must emit the **true** wait, and the client must be
  able to honour a long wait — the client-side 60 s clamp is tracked in the
  linked ContextHub item **WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM**.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Retry timer present and consistent:** A deterministic end-to-end test
  drives the in-process proxy with every provider unavailable and asserts the
  terminal `503` "All providers exhausted" response carries **both** a
  `Retry-After` HTTP header (integer delta-seconds) and a `retry_after` JSON body
  field, with the **same value**.
- **AC2 — Timeless truthfulness:** The asserted `retry_after` equals the real
  soonest availability (the maximum of cooldown durations, `available_times`
  window edges, and usage-limit reset times), is positive whenever a provider is
  genuinely blocked, and is `0` only when availability exists. The test pins the
  clock/value so the assertion is deterministic.
- **AC3 — Both exhaustion variants covered:** The verification covers the generic
  `code: "all_exhausted"` path and the time-window `code: "outside_time_window"`
  path (both are "All providers exhausted" 503s), asserting the same retry-timer
  contract on each.
- **AC4 — Client-recognition contract intact:** The response retains
  `error == "All providers exhausted"` and a stable `code`, and the existing
  exhaustion-contract tests still pass (additive-only; no prose/code change).
- **AC5 — No hold longer than the timer:** When a chain-hold would exceed the
  retry timer, the exhaustion response is surfaced immediately with the timer
  rather than held beyond it (bounded by `retry_after`). Verified in the same or
  a paired test.
- **AC6 — Client gap linked:** The ContextHub item WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM exists and
  is referenced from this item, so the proxy's honest multi-hour timer can be
  honoured by the client rather than clamped to 60 s.
- **AC7 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, `proxy/README.md` (the exhaustion/retry
  contract section), and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- **AC8 — Full suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Additive-only contract:** do not remove or reword the existing `error` prose
  or `code` values — older clients key on them (epic constraint
  LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO).
- **Verification, not availability policy:** do not widen `available_times` or
  wake a provider outside its window to make a test pass.
- **No proxy restart:** verification runs in-process; never kill the proxy.
- **Out of scope:** local slot-exhaustion 429, router concurrency-limit 503,
  compaction-gate 429, session single-flight 429 (per Q2); client code changes
  (ContextHub, per Q3).

## Existing state

- `_build_exhausted_response` and `_build_time_window_exhausted_response`
  (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`) emit `Retry-After` + `retry_after` on the 503,
  plus retained `error`/`code`/`diagnostics`/`unavailable_providers`.
- `_compute_retry_after` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`) computes the honest value
  from cooldowns (`_provider_unavailable_until`), `available_times` window edges
  (`_seconds_until_next_window`), and usage-limit resets (`_usage_reset_at`).
- `_bounded_chain_hold_seconds` / `_exhaustion_retry_after`
  (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`) bound the chain-hold by the response's real
  `Retry-After` and surface the response immediately when the timer exceeds the
  hold budget (LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08).
- The epic's integration verification item LP-0MUI68NTH004SZMG (blocked) already
  composes overnight remotes-out-of-window + usage-limit quarantine + local-lease
  denial and asserts an accurate 503; the retry timer is one of its assertions.
  This item's focused retry-timer verification should reference or extend that
  test rather than duplicate it (see Risks).
- Client side (ContextHub `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/`):
  `retry-logic.ts` parses `Retry-After`/`Retry-After-Ms` headers and the body
  `retry_after`, but clamps the applied delay to `maxDelayMs = 60000`; the retry
  loop (`register-recovery.ts`) is otherwise unbounded.

## Desired change

1. Add one deterministic end-to-end proxy test (or extend LP-0MUI68NTH004SZMG's
   test) proving the composed "All providers exhausted" retry contract:
   truthful `Retry-After` + `retry_after`, both exhaustion variants, no
   over-long hold, client-recognition prose/code intact.
2. Reference the linked ContextHub item WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM from this item (and
   vice versa) so the client-side 60 s clamp is tracked.
3. Update `proxy/README.md` (and code comments) to state the verified contract
   and the client expectation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_build_exhausted_response` (~line 2955),
  `_build_time_window_exhausted_response` (~line 3015), `_compute_retry_after`
  (~line 2257), `_bounded_chain_hold_seconds` / `_exhaustion_retry_after`
  (~line 4910).
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`, `proxy/tests/test_exhaustion_error_code.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_retry_after_bound.py` — extend/add the E2E
  retry-timer assertions.
- `proxy/README.md` — exhaustion / retry contract section (~line 690).
- Cross-repo: ContextHub `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts`
  (the linked item WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM, not edited here).

## Related work

| Item | Relationship |
|------|-------------|
| LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO — Epic: Overnight remote-chain exhaustion | Parent context; delivered the proxy-side retry contract this item verifies. |
| LP-0MUI68NTH004SZMG — E2E verification: overnight-gap exhaustion contract | Related/blocks: composes the overnight-gap 503; this item's retry-timer verification should reference/extend it, not duplicate it. |
| LP-0MT654ISW002QVH4 — Honest Retry-After: emit real provider availability windows | Predecessor: truthful `retry_after`/`Retry-After` on the exhaustion 503. |
| LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G — Exhaustion 503: stable machine-readable error code | Predecessor: `code` discriminators. |

# Objective

De-duplicate the `proxy-usage-analysis` local-skip / demand counters by
parsing `chain_hold_cycle` and excluding `chain_hold_cycle > 0` re-emissions
from the demand aggregates, while surfacing them separately as hold-cycle
re-emission activity.

## Problem statement

LP-0MU5AIAAY003KVM0 added a `chain_hold_cycle=<N>` field to the proxy's
`routing_check` / `routing_skip_local` / `compaction_bypass_eval` /
hold-start log lines so a single held request re-emitted across chain-hold
cycles is distinguishable from genuine new client demand. The
`proxy-usage-analysis` consumer has not been updated: `aggregation.py`
increments `hourly_activity[hour]['local_skip']` (and appends to
`routing_skip_events`, per-session `routing_skips`, and
`routing_skip_reason_counts`) for **every** `routing_skip` event, so a held
request that re-emits its skip once per cycle (up to `chain_hold_max_cycles`)
is counted N+1 times — inflating the local-skip / demand counters and making
one held request read as repeated client retries.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / agent analyst** reading the daily `proxy-usage-analysis`
  report: needs the "Local-skip" numbers and the
  `## routing_skip_local reasons` table to reflect genuine client demand, not
  chain-hold re-emissions.
- **Downstream JSON consumer** (dashboard / automated agent) querying
  `summary_to_json()` per-hour activity: needs the same de-duplication, plus a
  way to see hold-cycle re-emission volume separately.

Example user stories:

- As an operator, when a session is held through N chain-hold cycles, I want
  its local-skip counted once so my fallback/demand ratios are accurate.
- As an operator, I want to see that a request was re-emitted N times by the
  hold cycle (separately from demand) so I can tell a stuck hold from a client
  retry storm.

## Existing state

- Producer side (shipped, LP-0MU5AIAAY003KVM0): `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
  emits `chain_hold_cycle=<N>` on the `routing_check`, `routing_skip_local`,
  and `compaction_bypass_eval` INFO lines and on the hold-start WARNING line.
  Cycle 0 is the first (pre-hold) cycle; every hold-restart increments it.
- Consumer side (unchanged): `log_parser.py` recognises only
  `routing_skip_local` among those lines and does not parse
  `chain_hold_cycle`; `aggregation.aggregate` counts every `routing_skip`
  event identically, regardless of cycle.
- The existing `ROUTING_SKIP_*` test fixtures predate the field (no
  `chain_hold_cycle` token), so pre-chain-hold log lines must keep parsing.

## Desired change

- Parse `chain_hold_cycle=<N>` in `log_parser.py` into a new
  `LogEvent.chain_hold_cycle: int | None` field (tolerant: absent → `None`).
- In `aggregation.py`, exclude `routing_skip` events with
  `chain_hold_cycle > 0` from the demand / local-skip counters and aggregates,
  while recording them separately as hold-cycle re-emission activity.
- Surface the separate hold-cycle activity in the report/JSON.
- Add parser/aggregation/reporting tests covering a held request across
  cycles, plus a backward-compatibility test for logs without the field.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `log_parser.parse_log_line` populates `LogEvent.chain_hold_cycle` with the
   integer parsed from `chain_hold_cycle=N` on a `routing_skip_local` line, and
   leaves it `None` when the token is absent (pre-chain-hold log lines).
   Verified by parser unit tests using new fixtures with and without the token.
2. `aggregation.aggregate` counts a single held request re-emitted across
   cycles exactly once in `hourly_activity[...]['local_skip']`,
   `routing_skip_events`, per-session `routing_skips`, and
   `routing_skip_reason_counts` (the cycle-0 occurrence), while the new
   hold-cycle re-emission activity (`hold_cycle_routing_skip_events` and its
   count) reflects the `chain_hold_cycle > 0` occurrences. Verified by an
   aggregation test feeding one cycle-0 and three cycle>0 events for the same
   session.
3. The operator report and `summary_to_json()` surface the hold-cycle
   re-emission activity as its own metric and exclude it from the
   `routing_skip_local reasons` counts and the local-skip percentage
   denominators. Verified by a reporting test.
4. Backward compatibility: log lines without `chain_hold_cycle` (older rotated
   logs) are treated as cycle 0, so all pre-existing routing-skip tests and
   aggregates are unchanged. Verified by the existing suite plus a new
   explicit no-field test.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `SKILL.md`, and any relevant docs-site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Repository boundary (recorded exception):** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/`
  is agent-infrastructure, normally off-limits per AGENTS.md; this work item
  explicitly authorises changes confined to that skill's `scripts/` and
  `tests/` (and its `SKILL.md`). No other agent-infrastructure directories are
  touched.
- **No proxy-side changes:** the log field is already produced by
  `proxy/proxy/provider.py`; this task is consumer-only.
- Parsing must remain tolerant/unfatal: a missing or malformed
  `chain_hold_cycle` must never drop a line (default to `None`/cycle 0).

## Assumptions (documented; no operator response required)

- **A1 — absent field = cycle 0.** Pre-chain-hold log lines and any line
  missing the token are treated as genuine demand (cycle 0). This preserves
  historic counts and avoids silently discarding real skips.
- **A2 — exclude from counters, surface separately.** `chain_hold_cycle > 0`
  events are removed from every demand/local-skip aggregate (hourly
  `local_skip`, `routing_skip_events`, per-session `routing_skips`,
  `routing_skip_reason_counts`, and the report reasons table/percentages) and
  recorded instead in a dedicated hold-cycle re-emission list/counter. This is
  the union of the item's "exclude (or flag)" wording and matches the stated
  intent of "still surfacing them as hold-cycle activity".
- **A3 — scope limited to parsed `routing_skip` events.** `routing_check` and
  `compaction_bypass_eval` are not parsed today and feed no counters; parsing
  them (and adding demand counters over `routing_check`) is out of scope to
  avoid scope creep. The new `LogEvent` field is nonetheless generic so a
  future parser addition can reuse it.
- **A4 — the "demand counter" is the local-skip activity.** The only
  re-emitted event that reaches a counter is `routing_skip_local`;
  `stream_started`/`requests_started` is not re-emitted by hold cycles, so it
  is already unaffected. "demand counters" in the title is read as the
  counters that proxy genuine demand (local-skip).

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — add
  `RE_CHAIN_HOLD_CYCLE`, the `LogEvent.chain_hold_cycle` field, and populate it
  when parsing `routing_skip_local` (docs/comments updated).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — split
  `routing_skip` handling on `chain_hold_cycle > 0`; new
  `AnalysisResult.hold_cycle_routing_skip_events` and a
  `hold_cycle_reemission_count` property; keep cycle-0 events in existing
  aggregates.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — surface hold-cycle
  re-emissions separately (report line/section + `summary_to_json()` field)
  and ensure the reasons table/percentages use only genuine skips.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` — add `routing_skip_local`
  fixtures with `chain_hold_cycle=0` and `>0`.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — parser,
  aggregation, reporting, and backward-compatibility tests.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` — document the field and the
  demand-vs-re-emission distinction.

## Related work

- Parent discovery: **LP-0MU5AIAAY003KVM0** — "Chain-hold cycles re-run
  provider resolution but never re-run session handling / compaction"
  (completed; shipped the `chain_hold_cycle` log field).
- Epic: **LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO** — "Overnight remote-chain exhaustion: accurate
  diagnostics, quarantine visibility, bounded chain-hold" (open) — explicitly
  calls out the downstream observability requirement this item implements.
- Producer code: `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`_log_chain_hold_start`,
  `routing_check`, `routing_skip_local`, `compaction_bypass_eval`).
- Consumer code: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/{log_parser,aggregation,reporting}.py`.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Report count drop is intended but visible.** Local-skip totals fall for
  windows containing held requests; document in the report/SKILL.md so the
  change is not mistaken for lost data.
- **Over-exclusion risk.** If a genuine new request ever carried
  `chain_hold_cycle > 0` it would be dropped; cycle is per-request state set
  by `_set_chain_hold_cycle`, so this cannot occur — covered by an aggregation
  test asserting cycle 0 is retained.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Parsing `routing_check` / `compaction_bypass_eval` or
  adding new demand counters is tempting; recorded here as out of scope
  (A3) and to be raised as a separate work item if needed.
- **Backward-compat risk.** Malformed/absent field must not crash or drop the
  line; covered by the tolerant-parse + no-field tests.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No blocking clarifying questions were raised during this intake — the seed
context (problem, change, references) was sufficient to draft a testable
brief. The following non-blocking design choices were resolved by the agent
with documented assumptions (see Assumptions A1–A4); the operator may override
any of them at review:

- Q: Exclude or flag `chain_hold_cycle > 0` events? — **Resolved: exclude from
  demand/local-skip counters, surface separately** (A2). Source: this intake's
  documented assumption, consistent with the item's "exclude (or flag) …
  while still surfacing them as hold-cycle activity".
- Q: Treat an absent `chain_hold_cycle` as demand? — **Resolved: yes, cycle 0**
  (A1). Source: documented assumption preserving historic counts.
- Q: Extend to `routing_check` / `compaction_bypass_eval`? — **Resolved: no**
  (A3), out of scope. Source: documented assumption; they feed no counters.

- **LP-0MTJET4R5002U1FW** – Test: Contented queue invariants regression (completed)

# Restart signature should hash the merged config (base + overlay)

Seed: discovered during LP-0MUI680CC007WLZ5 (F6, start-proxy config reads), parent LP-0MU0W548B0029255 (config merge + dedup).

## Problem statement

`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` decides whether to preserve the co-located llama-server across a `--restart` by comparing a sha256 of the **raw** mode config file (`config-fast.yaml` / `config-cheap.yaml`) against the value recorded in `proxy/.llama_server_signature.json`. Since the config dedup (LP-0MUI67ZNM008627E) made the mode files overlays, base-inherited local-backend settings (e.g. `local_model_ctx_size`, `session_slot_pool_size`, `llama_server_port`) no longer appear in them, so a base-only change to `proxy/config.yaml` no longer changes the hash and a `--restart` can wrongly **preserve** a llama-server whose effective config actually changed (stale warm cache / wrong slot pool).

## Users

- **Operator / DevOps** — edits `proxy/config.yaml` (or a mode overlay), runs `start-proxy.sh --restart`, and expects the co-located llama-server to be restarted exactly when the *effective* local-backend config changed, and preserved (warm KV/prompt cache retained) when it did not.
  - _"As an operator, after changing `server.local_model_ctx_size` in the base config I want `--restart` to respawn llama-server with the new context, not silently keep the old one."_
  - _"As an operator, when I restart only the proxy (no config change) I want the warm llama-server preserved so the next request does not pay a cold-prefill cost."_
- **Agent workers / start-proxy consumers** — depend on the running local backend matching the config they believe is active; a wrongly preserved server serves the wrong parallel-slot layout and context window.
- **Maintainers / tests** — need the restart-signature decision to be exercised without touching live processes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Single merged-config signature.** The restart signature is derived from the effective (merged) config (`proxy/config.yaml` base + selected mode overlay) through one shared, canonical hashing helper, so the shell read path (`start-proxy.sh`) and the Python write path (`lifecycle._config_file_sha256`) produce **byte-identical** hashes for the same config inputs.
- **AC2 — Base-only change forces a restart.** A base-only change that affects the local backend (e.g. `server.local_model_ctx_size`, `server.session_slot_pool_size`, `server.llama_server_port`) changes the signature, so `--restart` does **not** preserve the running llama-server (`KEEP_LLAMA=0`; llama-server is killed/restarted).
- **AC3 — Unchanged merged config preserves warmth.** An unchanged merged config still matches the recorded signature, so `--restart` preserves the warm llama-server (`KEEP_LLAMA=1`; the server is not killed) — the existing LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN behaviour is retained.
- **AC4 — Overlay-only change still restarts (regression guard).** A mode-overlay-only change (e.g. `session_slot_pool_size` in `config-cheap.yaml`) changes the signature and forces a restart, as it does today.
- **AC5 — Test coverage.** `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` covers both the base-only-change and unchanged-merged-config cases (preserve vs restart) using a sandboxed `--restart` run that intercepts `pkill`/`fuser`/`uvicorn` (no live processes); the shared hash helper is covered by `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` and the write-side value by `proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py`.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically `proxy/README.md` (base + overlay config model / `LLAMA_PROXY_CONFIG`) must state that the restart signature hashes the **merged** config, not the raw overlay file.
- **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Shell ⇄ Python hash parity.** `start-proxy.sh` reads the signature and the proxy writes it; both must use the identical canonicalisation or every restart will mismatch. The shared helper must be dependency-light (stdlib + `yaml`) so the shell can import it via a small inline `python -c` snippet, matching the existing `resolve_api_keys` pattern (`sys.path.insert(0, "$REPO_ROOT/proxy")`).
- **Merge semantics are fixed.** `deep_merge` is a recursive dict merge; overlay scalars/lists/`null` replace base wholesale (lists are never merged element-wise). The hash must reflect these effective values.
- **Backward compatibility.** Existing `proxy/.llama_server_signature.json` files hold a raw-file hash. After the change the first `--restart` will see a mismatch and conservatively restart llama-server once; this is acceptable (fail-safe direction) and should be noted in code comments.
- **`REPO_ROOT` is the `proxy/` directory** in `start-proxy.sh` (`SCRIPT_DIR/..`), despite the name; the base config is `$REPO_ROOT/config.yaml` and the signature file is `$REPO_ROOT/.llama_server_signature.json` (= `proxy/.llama_server_signature.json`, gitignored).
- **No live-process killing in tests.** Shell tests must not run real `pkill`/`fuser` against the live proxy/llama-server/TTS; sandbox the run (fake `pkill`/`fuser`/`uvicorn` on `PATH`), consistent with the `LIVE_PORT_KILL_TESTS` opt-in convention.

## Existing state

- **Shell read side** (`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh`, ~L160–190): derives `_restart_mode` from `proxy/.mode`, sets `_restart_cfg=config-<mode>.yaml` (falling back to `config.yaml`), and compares `sha256sum "$_restart_cfg"` against `signature.config_sha256`; when mode **and** hash match it sets `KEEP_LLAMA=1`. Hashing the raw overlay misses base-only keys.
- **Python write side** (`proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`): `_config_file_sha256()` sha256's the raw `LLAMA_PROXY_CONFIG` file; `_write_llama_server_signature()` stores it as `config_sha256` alongside `mode`/`model`/`parallel`/`router_mode`.
- **Adoption path** (`_try_adopt_running_llama_server`, lifecycle.py ~L131): adopts a running server when `router_mode` and `model` match; it does **not** compare `config_sha256` today. (See Risks — related gap, out of scope.)
- **Merge helper** (`proxy/proxy/config_merge.py`): `deep_merge`, `load_yaml_config`, `load_merged(base_path, overlay_path)`; already used by `start-proxy.sh` `resolve_api_keys` and by `proxy.utils._load_merged_config`.
- **Configs**: `proxy/config.yaml` base holds `local_model_ctx_size: 262144`, `session_slot_pool_size: 1`, `llama_server_port: 8080`, `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold: 38000`; `config-fast.yaml` overrides only model provider availability, `config-cheap.yaml` overrides ~8 server keys (e.g. `session_slot_pool_size: 3`, cold threshold `42000`). Neither overlay carries `local_model_ctx_size` / `llama_server_port` / `session_slot_pool_size` (fast).
- **Live signature** on this checkout currently records `config_sha256: ""` (the running process did not have `LLAMA_PROXY_CONFIG` set), which already fails the match and forces a restart — the safe fallback.

## Desired change

1. **Add a shared canonical hash helper** to `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py`, e.g. `merged_config_sha256(base_path, overlay_path) -> str`, computing `sha256(json.dumps(load_merged(base, overlay), sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode())`. Deterministic key ordering makes it stable across Python runs and independent of YAML formatting/comments (only effective values matter).
2. **Shell read side**: replace the raw `sha256sum "$_restart_cfg"` with an inline `"$PY_BIN" -c` call importing `merged_config_sha256` from `$REPO_ROOT/proxy` and hashing `($REPO_ROOT/config.yaml, $_restart_cfg)`. Preserve the existing guard: when the overlay file is absent, fall back to `config.yaml` (merged base with itself). Keep the fail-safe behaviour when `sha256sum`/Python is unavailable (empty hash ⇒ do not preserve).
3. **Python write side**: make `lifecycle._config_file_sha256()` resolve base = `<proxy>/config.yaml` and overlay = `$LLAMA_PROXY_CONFIG` (fallback to base if unset/missing) and return `merged_config_sha256(base, overlay)`; keep the `try/except → ""` best-effort contract.
4. **Tests**: extend `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` with sandboxed `--restart` cases (base-only change ⇒ kill; unchanged ⇒ preserve; fake `pkill`/`fuser`/`uvicorn`); add `merged_config_sha256` determinism/sensitivity tests to `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py`; assert the write-side value equals the shared helper in `proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py`.
5. **Docs/comments**: update `proxy/README.md` (config model / `LLAMA_PROXY_CONFIG` / restart lifecycle) and the `start-proxy.sh` and `lifecycle.py` comments to state the signature hashes the merged config, with the one-time conservative-restart note.

- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` — restart-gate read side (raw → merged hash); comment update.
- `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` — new `merged_config_sha256` shared canonical helper.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — `_config_file_sha256()` write side uses the shared helper; comment update.
- `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` — sandboxed `--restart` preserve/kill cases (AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5).
- `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` — helper determinism + base/overlay sensitivity.
- `proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py` — write-side hash equals the shared helper.
- `proxy/README.md` — config model + restart-signature documentation.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — canonicalisation choice is free.** JSON-with-sorted-keys over the merged dict is assumed acceptable; it intentionally ignores comments/formatting, so only semantic config changes trigger a restart. If byte-for-byte raw merged YAML is preferred, the same helper can serialise differently, but both sides must change together.
- **Risk — hash drift between shell and Python.** If either side uses a different serialisation/path, signatures never match and *every* restart cold-starts llama-server. AC1 and the Python test guard against this.
- **Risk — silent wrong-config adoption on non-`--restart` starts.** `_try_adopt_running_llama_server` still ignores `config_sha256`, so a plain start (or router self-heal path) could adopt a server whose config changed. - **Assumption — one-time conservative restart is acceptable.** Pre-upgrade signature files mismatch once; operators see a single extra llama-server restart. Documented, not mitigated.

# Raise Qwen3 cache-ram to 40,960 MiB

Follow-up to LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW (which verified the 32,768 MiB cap on the
live post-deploy window) and LP-0MUYFC3C5004TCYN.

## Context

The 2026-10-12 post-32-GiB verification
(`docs/dev/prompt-cache-post-deploy-2026-10-12.json`) showed the cache is
still saturating under the current single-slot load:

- 18 evictions over ~4.7 d (1.28% of requests; 65 -> 18 vs the length-matched
  8 GiB window, a 72.9%/req reduction);
- 26.3% of cache-state samples above 90% of the 32,768 MiB cap (vs 22.0% at
  8 GiB);
- observed maximum 16 concurrently-retained prompts, cache peak 32,765.6 MiB
  (fully saturated).

`scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py --recommend` over that measurement derives
**40,960 MiB (40 GiB)**:

    per-prompt state 2,013 MiB x observed max 16 x 1.25 margin = 40,260 MiB
    -> round up to 40,960 MiB (holds ~20 prompts >= observed 16)

Headroom is safe (host available 79,248 MiB - 40,960 = 38,288 MiB, well above
the 12,743.7 MiB reserve = max(8 GiB, 10% MemTotal)), so the
`server_prompt_cache::alloc()` OOM fallback (`limit_size = 0.4 * size()`) is
not approached.

## Goal

As a proxy operator, raise the Qwen3 prompt-cache cap to the derived
40,960 MiB so the cache stops saturating and evicting session prefixes under
the single-slot load, with the derivation and headroom recorded.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `models.ini` `[Qwen3]` `cache-ram` raised 32768 -> 40960, with the
   derivation (per-prompt 2,013 MiB x observed max 16 x 1.25) and the
   2026-10-12 measurement reference recorded in the comment block.
2. Headroom invariant re-checked at 40,960 MiB: MemAvailable - 40960 >= reserve
   (reserve = max(8 GiB, 10% MemTotal)); the OOM fallback path is documented
   as avoided.
3. Deploy via `/skill:start-proxy --restart` (never kill the proxy manually);
   confirm the spawned Qwen3 child carries `--cache-ram 40960` (and
   `--ctx-checkpoints 32`, no `--swa-full`).
4. `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` updated with the new cap, the derivation
   and the deploy evidence.
5. Full project test suite passes.

## Non-goals

- Changing `ctx-checkpoints` / `checkpoint-every-n-tokens` (kept at 32; the
  checkpoint term is not the lever, see `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md`).
- Re-tuning routing cold/warm thresholds.
- The live post-deploy validation of this change (separate follow-up).

No client supplies the content client-side, so the prompt currently has zero effect — the completed LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE deliverable is unreachable through the proxy's auto-loading path.

## Users

- **Wiki authoring operators** invoking the `author` alias (directly or via an authoring client) — they expect the mandatory wiki guidelines to shape every `author` response.
- **Readers of the open_source_llm wiki** — indirectly benefit from consistent openness terminology, citation, and naming conventions.

Example user stories:

- As an operator authoring wiki content via the `author` alias, I want the proxy to inject `proxy/prompts/author.txt` into my requests so that terminology/openness classification and citation rules are applied without me having to paste the guidelines each time.
- As a wiki reader, I want model categories consistently labelled (open-source vs open-weights vs closed) and project/concept names explained at first mention (LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE) so pages are accurate and navigable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `proxy/config.yaml` gains a `system_prompt` block on the `author` entry with `mode: "override"` and `file: "proxy/prompts/author.txt"`, and config validation passes at load time.
- [ ] A test asserts `resolve_system_prompt("author", model_cfg)` against the real config returns the author.txt content (mode `override`, correct `source` path); an injection-path test asserts an `author` request's system messages are replaced by author.txt content (mode `override`).
- [ ] The proxy auto-loading path is verified live: a `model=author` request through `proxy_openai_api` applies the resolved prompt (first real-world use of the `system_prompt` feature).
- [ ] Documentation is updated to reflect the wiring, including `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` (author as a worked `system_prompt` example) and code comments as needed.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes (build → test → commit order).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Keep the `system_prompt` schema as documented in `proxy/config.yaml` (lines 113–127): optional block, `mode` ∈ {override, prepend} (required), `file` relative to repo root.
- Resolution precedence must be preserved: local override (`.sorraAgents/prompts/author.txt`, currently absent) → repo default (`proxy/prompts/author.txt`).
- `author.txt` must stay within the resolver's max file size (64 KB); content changes are out of scope here (author.txt content is owned by LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE / prompt-content work).

## Existing state

- `resolve_system_prompt()` (`proxy/proxy/prompt_resolver.py:82`) returns `None` when `model_cfg["system_prompt"]` is absent.

     system_prompt:
       mode: "override"   # operator-confirmed; replaces client system messages

**Type:** task (verification) · **Priority:** high

## Problem

The proxy already emits the composed "All providers exhausted" retry contract
(`Retry-After` header + matching `retry_after` body field, stable `code`, no
over-long chain-hold), but the existing end-to-end test
(`proxy/tests/test_overnight_exhaustion_e2e.py`, from LP-0MUI68NTH004SZMG) does
**not** pin the composed contract tightly enough to catch every regression:

- it asserts `retry_after > 0` and that the header matches the body, but never
  asserts the value **equals** the real soonest availability computed under a
  pinned clock (AC2);
- it exercises the generic `code: all_exhausted` path end-to-end, but the
  sole-cause time-window `code: outside_time_window` variant is asserted only
  against the response builder (`test_exhaustion_error_code.py`), not through
  the fallback chain with the retry timer (AC3);
- the client-recognition prose (`error == "All providers exhausted"`) and the
  bounded-hold guarantee are asserted, but not as one pinned regression for
  the retry timer (AC1, AC4, AC5).

## Change

Harden the end-to-end exhaustion test so the whole "no models available" retry
contract is pinned and fails if any part regresses. Extend the existing test
file — do **not** duplicate the window+quarantine or lease-denied scenarios.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Retry timer present and consistent:** A deterministic end-to-end test
  drives the in-process proxy with every provider unavailable and asserts the
  terminal `503` "All providers exhausted" response carries **both** a
  `Retry-After` HTTP header (integer delta-seconds) and a `retry_after` JSON body
  field, with the **same value**.
- **AC2 — Timeless truthfulness:** The asserted `retry_after` equals the real
  soonest availability (the maximum of cooldown durations, `available_times`
  window edges, and usage-limit reset times), is positive whenever a provider is
  genuinely blocked, and is `0` only when availability exists. The test pins the
  clock/value so the assertion is deterministic.
- **AC3 — Both exhaustion variants covered:** The verification covers the generic
  `code: "all_exhausted"` path and the time-window `code: "outside_time_window"`
  path (both are "All providers exhausted" 503s), asserting the same retry-timer
  contract on each.
- **AC4 — Client-recognition contract intact:** The response retains
  `error == "All providers exhausted"` and a stable `code`, and the existing
  exhaustion-contract tests still pass (additive-only; no prose/code change).
- **AC5 — No hold longer than the timer:** When a chain-hold would exceed the
  retry timer, the exhaustion response is surfaced immediately with the timer
  rather than held beyond it (bounded by `retry_after`). Verified in the same or
  a paired test.
- **AC8 — Full suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `proxy/tests/test_overnight_exhaustion_e2e.py`: reuse `_FixedDateTime`, `_DummyRequest`, the provider-state reset fixture and the `_record_hold` monkeypatch already in the file.
- Add a sole-cause window case with all providers outside `available_times` and no cooldown/quarantine, asserting `code == "outside_time_window"` plus the matching `Retry-After`/`retry_after`.
- For the window+quarantine case, pin the expected value (window edge in seconds under `_FixedDateTime`) and assert `retry_after == <expected>` exactly, that `_compute_retry_after` under the same clock equals it, and that the header equals the body string.
- Assert the `0` edge case (`_build_exhausted_response()` with no blockers → `retry_after == 0`).
- Keep determinism: monkeypatch `_hold_sleep` to record; assert no real sleep.
- No code change to `proxy/proxy/provider.py` is expected; if a genuine gap is found, raise a bug work item and record the blocking relationship instead of widening scope.

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_overnight_exhaustion_e2e.py` — the extended E2E retry-timer assertions (primary).
- `proxy/tests/test_honest_retry_after.py` — reuse its pinned-clock expectations for the window-edge arithmetic.
- `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_retry_after_bound.py` — reference for the bounded-hold assertions.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — read-only reference: `_compute_retry_after` (~2383), `_build_exhausted_response` (~3177), `_build_time_window_exhausted_response` (~3241).

## Deliverables

- Test diff with the pinned retry-timer assertions for both exhaustion variants and the bounded-hold guarantee.
- Recorded test-run output (targeted file + full suite) as evidence on this work item.

# Fix accidentally committed broken proxy/node_modules symlink (re-introduced)

## Problem statement

The repository tracks `proxy/node_modules` as a broken self-referential git symlink (`proxy/node_modules → /home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy/node_modules`), which breaks `npm install` and Playwright runs inside `proxy/`. The symlink was previously removed in LP-0MUIH7FYS0010MLT (commit a45bb99f) with a .gitignore hardening, but was re-introduced by commit b6c238ed.

## Users

- **LLM operators / proxy developers** — Cannot run `npm install` or Playwright tests in `proxy/` without a manual workaround.
- **Map (agent/auditor)** — Automated tooling fails when operating in `proxy/`.

## Existing state

- `proxy/node_modules` is tracked as mode 120000 (symlink) pointing to itself — a broken loop.
- `proxy/.gitignore` was hardened in a45bb99f to ignore `node_modules` (symlink form), but the symlink was re-committed in b6c238ed.
- Root cause: the implement framework's `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` auto-symlinks `node_modules` from the main checkout into worktrees; if the symlink lands in a commit, the .gitignore pattern does not prevent it from being tracked (git adds what's staged, regardless of .gitignore).
- A related framework concern was noted in LP-0MUIH7FYS0010MLT's closing comment.

## Desired change

Remove `proxy/node_modules` from git tracking and prevent recurrence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1:** `git ls-files | grep node_modules` returns no results — no `node_modules` entries tracked in any branch.
2. **AC2:** `proxy/node_modules` does not appear in `git status` after any `implement.py start` / `implement.py finish` cycle.
3. **AC3:** `npm install` can run successfully in `proxy/` without pre-existing symlinks or workarounds.
4. **AC4:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. **AC5:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The implement framework's `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` mechanism must not re-introduce tracked symlinks.
- Solution must work across all branches (not just `dev`).
- Avoid broad `.gitignore` changes that might affect other legitimate symlink tracking.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/.gitignore` — May need further hardening to cover edge cases.
- `scripts/implement.py` (SorraAgents) — The `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` function may need to exclude symlinks from staging.
- `.gitignore` (main checkout) — Consider adding `proxy/node_modules` at the repo root level.
- `proxy/package.json` — Verify `npm install` works post-fix.

## Related work

- **LP-0MUIH7FYS0010MLT** — "Remove accidentally committed proxy/node_modules symlink; harden gitignore" (completed, a45bb99f) — previously removed this symlink and hardened `proxy/.gitignore`, but it was re-introduced.

## Goal

Raise the fast-mode large-context routing thresholds so the 46.6%-of-fallbacks `large_context_bypass` band (3,773 events, 99.9% fast) and part of the `context_too_large` band are admitted to the single fast slot, increasing local capture and busy time.

## Context (from parent LP-0MV8805WF007LTZA)

Fast profile today (1 slot × 262,144 ctx):
- COLD `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold` = **38,000** (economic new-token threshold; skip reason `large_context_bypass` when a full re-prefill looks expensive) — NOTE: fast does NOT set `local_large_context_economic_bypass_serves_local`, so economic bypasses fall back to remote.
- WARM = `min(physical 258,048, economic)`, economic = `min(round(0.3815 × 262144) = 100,008, absolute 100,000)` = **100,000** (skip reason `context_too_large`).

Worked examples are in the parent item (Examples 1–6, 8). Key messages:

1. **The cold threshold is the binding fast-mode constraint.** Sessions with `est` in (38k, 100k] and a cold cache (cached_ratio ≈ 0, e.g. after the 01:00/10:00 restart) hit `large_context_bypass` at the full prefill cost. Raising COLD moves that band to local unconditionally.
2. **Raising the ratio alone is INERT** — the absolute `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold: 100000` caps the economic term (Example 4: ratio 0.45 → 117,965 → min(117,965, 100,000) = 100,000; ratio 0.55 → 144,179 → 100,000). WARM must be raised by raising **both** the ratio and the absolute cap.

## Change

`proxy/config-fast.yaml` (overlay):

```yaml
server:
  local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold: 55000
  local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio: 0.55
  local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold: 144179
```

Resulting fast thresholds (verified arithmetic): physical = 258,048; economic = min(round(0.55 × 262144) = 144,179, 144,179) = 144,179; effective WARM = **144,179**; COLD = **55,000**. The (55k, 144k] band stays non-empty (LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP constraint).

- [ ] `proxy/config-fast.yaml` updated with the three values in the worktree (build → test → commit order); update the golden fixtures and any tests asserting the fast profile thresholds. ## Goal

Determine how often the llama-proxy flips between **fast** and **cheap** modes,
what triggers each flip (in particular the ContextHub/herdr code that initiates
the switch to fast), whether the flip rate is problematic, and what (if
anything) should change to reduce it.

## Context / findings so far

Investigation of the 24h window 2026-10-14 14:02 → 2026-10-15 14:02 UTC found
**30 proxy restarts**, of which **15 were "Mode-switch restart spawned"**
(one restart per real mode transition).

Trigger sources identified:

- **ContextHub / herdr** — `../ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts`:
  - *Fast on command*: records operator activity and fire-and-forget
    `POST /admin/set-mode {"mode":"fast"}`.
  - *Cheap on idle*: leader-only, when idle ≥
    `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` (900_000 ms = 15 min) **and** the
    proxy reports idle, gated by the model-cooldown signal.
  - Shared activity broadcast via `mode-activity.json`; leader elected via the
    downtime worker; fail-closed everywhere.
- **Proxy's built-in time schedule** — `proxy/mode_schedule.yaml`
  (cheap 01:00, fast 10:00) = 2/day.
- **Manual** `POST /admin/set-mode` (operators/agents).

Each real transition persists the mode and spawns
`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart` (`proxy/proxy/mode.py` `set_mode()` →
`_spawn_restart()`), because fast/cheap are separate config profiles
(`config-fast.yaml` vs `config-cheap.yaml`) with different slot-pool sizes
(fast: base `session_slot_pool_size: 1`; cheap: 3). The restart re-inits
llama-server and typically yields a ~60s local-qwen3 cooldown on a cold-start
503. Redundant switches are skipped (mode already matches), so transition count
== restart-contribution count.

**Is this period unusual?** Historical per-calendar-day mode-switch counts from
the rotated logs: 10-08=28, 10-09=22, 10-10=16, 10-11=10, 10-12=32, 10-13=24,
10-14=31, 10-15=19 (partial, ~14h). So flipping is **endemic (~10–34/day)** —
to be confirmed and extended in this investigation.

## Questions to answer

1. How many flips/day, split by trigger source (ContextHub fast-on-command,
   ContextHub idle-cheap, proxy schedule, manual)?
2. Is the fast-on-command path firing repeatedly during active periods
   (flip-flop)? Quantify fast→cheap→fast pairs within short windows.
3. What is the cost per flip (restart duration, local cooldown, dropped or
   retried in-flight work, cold-prefill thunder)?
4. What else (besides mode) causes the proxy to restart, and how much of the
   flip rate is attributable to each?
5. What options exist to reduce flipping (e.g. minimum-dwell/hysteresis, keep
   fast during working hours rather than idle-cheap, only switch when the
   benefit is real, coalesce/defer switches, non-destructive switch), with
   trade-offs?
6. Recommendation: act or not, and if so, what and with what measurable target?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Flip frequency over ≥7 days of logs is documented (per-day counts +
      intra-day distribution), separated by trigger source.
- [ ] The ContextHub `mode-switch-worker.ts` switching logic is documented
      (triggers, gates, thresholds, leader election, cooldown gate, fail-closed
      behaviour).
- [ ] A quantified answer to "was the studied 24h period unusual?" against the
      ≥7-day baseline.
- [ ] A cost-per-flip estimate (restart duration, local cooldown, in-flight
      impact, cold-prefill effect).
- [ ] A prioritised list of reduction options with expected effect and
      trade-offs, and at least one recommended option with a measurable target.
- [ ] Follow-up implementation work items are created for the recommended
      option(s), or a decision not to act is recorded.
- [ ] Evidence is command/log based and reproducible (exact greps/scripts
      recorded in this item).

  `../ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts`.

# Intake brief: Equalise fast/cheap slot counts (3/2/1) or keep the drain

Work item: LP-0MV9UNGEB009XUZ5 — Priority: medium — Type: task

## Problem statement

Switching between **fast** and **cheap** modes currently restarts the whole
proxy **and** llama-server, because the two profiles differ in
`session_slot_pool_size` (fast/base = 1, cheap = 3). The restart discards the
warm KV cache and kills in-flight local streams. We need to know whether a
single slot count is viable for both modes — which would let a switch keep the
running llama-server (via the existing adopt/reuse path) — or whether the
per-mode slot count must stay and the already-implemented drain remains the
mitigation.

## Users

- **Agent operators / users** — long-running Pi sessions through the proxy; a
  mode switch today interrupts work and loses the warm cache, degrading the
  next requests' TTFT.
- **Proxy operators** — switch modes manually (UI/API) or on schedule
  (cheap 01:00–10:00, fast 10:00–01:00) and want the switch to be cheap and
  non-disruptive.
- **Benchmark / maintainer** — needs reproducible numbers to justify (or
  reject) a config change.

User stories:

- As an agent operator, I want a mode switch to preserve the warm local KV
  cache so my next request is not slowed by a cold restart.
- As a proxy operator, I want an evidence-based decision on whether fast and
  cheap can share one slot count, so the restart-on-switch can be removed (or
  knowingly retained).
- As a maintainer, I want the 1/2/3-slot trade-off quantified (per-slot
  context, memory, decode speed, contention) for the small-request workload the
  local slot actually serves.

## Acceptance criteria

- Benchmark results for 1, 2 and 3 slots are recorded with reproducible commands, configs and raw numbers, covering throughput, latency/TTFT, queue-timeout / `fallback_after_queue` rate, local stream share, and local quarantine episodes, at ≥ the observed concurrency (2–3 concurrent sessions plus queue depth).
- A recommendation states whether a single slot count is viable for both modes, the chosen N, and the measured trade-offs (per-slot context, memory, decode speed, contention including queue-timeout rate).
- The evaluation explicitly accounts for large-context bypass traffic (400–750/day, `large_context_bypass` / `context_too_large`) when interpreting the per-slot context trade-off — i.e. how much of the local-eligible traffic is small, and what per-slot context can be given up at higher N.
- If a single slot count is viable: a follow-up work item is created to converge `session_slot_pool_size` across `config.yaml` / `config-fast.yaml` / `config-cheap.yaml` and make the switch non-destructive by reusing the running llama-server (existing adopt path, LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN) rather than restarting it.
- If not viable: the recommendation documents why, confirms the already-implemented bounded drain (`server.mode_switch_drain`, LP-0MT631JKW008WAKE) remains the mitigation, and files any gaps found as follow-up items (`discovered-from:LP-0MV9UNGEB009XUZ5`).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes via `/skill:test`.

## Constraints

- The proxy serves concurrent production consumers; the benchmark must not
  permanently destabilise the running config. Any config edit during
  benchmarking must be reverted/restored, and the proxy left in the correct
  scheduled mode.
- Slot count must match llama-server `--parallel`; changing it requires a
  llama-server restart (the very cost under evaluation).
- fast = 1 slot × 262144 ctx; cheap = 3 slots × 262144 ctx. Per-slot context at
  N slots is roughly `ctx_size // N` minus output headroom (routing thresholds
  are auto-derived; see config comments).
- Benchmark scripts/artifacts live under `proxy/benchmarks/`; transient outputs
  must not leave tracked paths permanently dirty.

## Existing state

- `proxy/config.yaml` (base profile) `session_slot_pool_size: 1`;
  `proxy/config-fast.yaml` overrides other values but inherits 1;
  `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` sets `session_slot_pool_size: 3`.
- A mode switch is a full restart (`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart`)
  driven by `proxy/proxy/mode.py`; it also restarts llama-server, so the warm
  KV cache is lost.
- A **bounded drain already exists** (`mode.py`: `_begin_drain`, `draining()`,
  `drain_retry_after()`, `_count_in_flight_local_streams()`,
  `_wait_for_in_flight_local_streams()`, `_spawn_restart`), implemented under
  LP-0MT631JKW008WAKE (completed) and covered by
  `proxy/tests/test_mode_switch_drain.py`. It defers new chat requests
  (503 + Retry-After) and waits up to `mode_switch_drain.max_seconds`
  (fast 30s, cheap/base 90s). ⇒ the item's conditional "implement a drain"
  branch is already satisfied.
- llama-server reuse/adopt across a proxy-only restart exists in
  `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` (LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN), with
  `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` `merged_config_sha256` guarding against
  adopting a stale config.
- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` (LP-0MRWJIBIE0012HDD) varies
  1/2/4/6/8/12 slots and measures throughput/latency/TTFT/GPU memory. It does
  **not** currently report queue-timeout rate, local stream share, or
  quarantine episodes, and uses 6 concurrent requests — it may need extension
  for the concurrency/metrics this item requires.
- Contention evidence carried in the item: fast 1-slot 10:00–14:02 window →
  173 `fallback_after_queue`; cheap 3-slot 01:00–10:00 → 207 over a longer
  window; 39 `empty_response` cooldowns cluster under 1-slot contention.

## Desired change

Produce an evidence-backed verdict on a single slot count for both modes and
act on it:

- **Viable** → create a follow-up item to converge the configs and keep
  llama-server warm across the switch (adopt path); the mode switch becomes a
  proxy-only restart.
- **Not viable** → document why and keep the existing bounded drain; file any
  gaps as `discovered-from` follow-ups.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml` — base profile; `session_slot_pool_size: 1`; routing and
  context thresholds.
- `proxy/config-fast.yaml` — fast overlay; inherits slot count, sets
  `mode_switch_drain.max_seconds: 30`.
- `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — cheap overlay; `session_slot_pool_size: 3`.
- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` — existing slot sweep; candidate to
  extend with queue-timeout / local-share / quarantine metrics.
- `proxy/proxy/mode.py` — mode switch, bounded drain, `_spawn_restart`.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — llama-server reuse/adopt across proxy restart
  (LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN).
- `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` — `deep_merge` + `merged_config_sha256`
  stale-adopt guard.
- `proxy/tests/test_mode_switch_drain.py` — existing drain test coverage.
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_benchmark.py` — existing benchmark unit tests.

## Related work

- LP-0MRWJIBIE0012HDD — Slot-count benchmark: optimal `session_slot_pool_size`
  (completed; script reusable).
- LP-0MT631JKW008WAKE — Drain or re-route in-flight local streams at
  mode-switch restart (completed; drain implemented).
- LP-0MT60S55M000TK1H — Stream finish errors: recover-first reroute (completed;
  classified 4 restart-kill events).
- LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN — llama-server reuse across proxy-only restarts (adopt).
- LP-0MRW0WTOO002GG8I — pool 2 → 6 (completed).
- LP-0MQMH0WHY005UPFA — align pool with llama-server `--parallel`.
- LP-0MRDE669Y003V1SO — cache-cold after restart.
- LP-0MSM3TGO3007QN9M — mode control UI.
- LP-0MSMF5LXO006YDNM — in-flight sessions keep their models across mode
  switches (completed).
- LP-0MU5BOK3P0090O0V — mode flapping / switch restarts (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the benchmark can be run without permanently disrupting
  production; the config is restored and the proxy left in the correct
  scheduled mode afterwards.
- **Assumption:** the already-implemented bounded drain satisfies the item's
  conditional "if not viable: implement a drain" branch (see Existing state),
  so the remaining scope is evaluation → recommendation → follow-up items.
- **Risk:** benchmarking 3 × 262144 ctx may OOM or force a lower per-slot
  context, biasing results. Record memory and per-slot context, and treat
  OOM / severely reduced per-slot context as a viability failure.
- **Risk:** the benchmark workload may not match real traffic — large-context
  bypass dominates request counts but never touches the local slot. Characterise
  the local-eligible request mix explicitly.
- **Risk (scope creep):** tuning the drain, changing remote fallback policy, or
  UI changes are **out of scope** here — record as linked follow-up items
  rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (prior mode-flip
investigation) plus repository inspection (`mode.py`, `lifecycle.py`,
`config*.yaml`, `proxy/benchmarks/`, `proxy/tests/`) sufficed to draft the
brief. One interpretation was recorded as a documented assumption (see Risks &
assumptions): the already-implemented bounded drain satisfies the item's
conditional "implement a drain" branch, so the remaining work is evaluation →
recommendation → follow-up items.

- **LP-0MT1EE315007AKXG** – proxy-usage-analysis: recognize manual mode switches in mode timeline (completed)

- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: acceptance, accounts, active, align, already (+143 more)
